title: A Resolution-Agnostic Geometric Transformer for Chromosome Modeling Using Inertial Frame

split.decision: std3: preserve published chromosome groups; train 1,3,5,7,8,9,11,13,15,16,17,19,21,22,23; val 2,6,10,12; test 4,14,18,20. No random split. Opaque ids hide chromosome identity. Mapping operator-only. Materialized groups=15/4/4, real loci=17675/6700/4114; all source hashes and contact arrays verified; raw coordinates float32 bit-equal. No split seed.

allowed_changes: The refinement model, internal coordinate features, training surrogate, optimizer and hyperparameters may change; inference uses only the current structure and trained model.
fixed_contract: Refine the supplied LorDG chromosome structures to improve contact-derived geometric agreement.
The supplied LorDG coordinates, node indices, splits and contact-derived target distances are fixed.
The equal-structure dSCC objective, float32 padded 2400-slot distance normalization and dRMSE at most 0.095 on test and 0.12 on val remain fixed.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget
forbidden_substitutions: Real-locus coordinates must come from a trained refinement model; returning the supplied coordinates unchanged, or changed only by a rigid motion or a global scale, is not a valid submission.
Do not substitute another initial structure source, use contacts as prediction inputs, or change normalization, padding, metric or guard.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.
